summary: Analysing the benefits and restrictions of a new system, and the characteristics of software development frameworks.

blocks.content: When proposing a new system, the analyst explains how it will improve on the current one. Benefits should be **specific to the scenario** and, where possible, **measurable**.

blocks.title: Typical benefits
rows: Selling prices calculated instantly instead of by hand
Automatic calculation and validation — fewer mistakes in prices
Staff spend less time on paperwork
Data available on any device, anytime
Data protected by passwords and backed up, unlike paper records

blocks.content: "Describe three benefits" → each answer needs the **benefit + how it helps in this scenario**: "**Auto-calculation of the price** means staff **no longer make arithmetic mistakes** when adding the 30% mark-up."

blocks.title: Constraints that limit a new system
rows: The school can spend only 2 million tenge on hardware and software
The system must be ready before the new academic year
Must run on existing computers / older phones
Must work with the current database and operating system
Staff have little IT experience → training needed; interface must be simple
Must follow personal data protection law
Sensitive data limits what can be stored in the cloud
Some features are left for a later version

blocks.content: A **ready-made platform of reusable code, libraries, tools and rules** on which developers build applications, instead of writing everything from scratch.

items.title: Characteristics
items.content:
- Provides a **structure** (architecture, e.g. Model–View–Controller) that the code must follow.
- **Reusable components and libraries** (forms, database access, authentication).
- Built-in **security** features (input sanitising, CSRF protection).
- **Tools**: code generators, testing tools, package managers, debuggers.
- **Documentation** and a community.
- "**Inversion of control**" — the framework calls your code, not the other way round.

items.title: Examples
items.content:
- Web: **Laravel** (PHP), **Django**/Flask (Python), **React**, **Angular**, Vue (JavaScript), ASP.NET.
- Mobile: **Flutter**, React Native, Android SDK, SwiftUI.
- Desktop/games: .NET, Qt, Unity.

blocks.title: Using a framework
rows: Faster development — common features already written
Must follow its rules — less flexibility
Extra code may make the app larger or slower
Dependence on the framework's updates and lifespan
